main_text.p: V. Sed absurditatem longè omnem superat, quod tradidit Sixtus Senensis, Biblioth.Lib.vii.Cap.viii. tribuere quosdam Tertulliano. Quo commento post homines natos nullum insultius, impudentius nullum. Illos Epistolæ cothurnos aptari Tertulliano? Quem ante Justinus, Irenæus, Clemens uterque, Epistolam usurparunt totiens; qui Barnabæ ipsemet adscripsit; qui Timotheo, totâ ætate posterior; qui libro de Hæres. notat Theodotum, verba illa Epistolæ, apator, ametor, ageneologitus, cujus neque initium, neque finis, contorquentem; nec jam de phrasi Tertulliani diversâ toto coelo, ac Latinâ quidem eâ, & Africanâ, aliisque pro Epistolæ antiquitate dicam argumentis. Atque ita quod instituéramus primùm, plenissimè executos nos esse arbitramur. Omnibusque tandem æstimatis, authoritatibus omnibus expensis, rationibus libratis, instantiis excussis, exceptionibus eversis, id unum superesset, Pauli Epistolam ut esse credamus, credant quę nepotes.

page.notes: The running head, page number 263 and gathering signature are printed. The "V." opening the page is a paragraph number and is kept inside the paragraph. Printed hyphenations "u-surparunt" and "po-sterior" and "Theodo-tum" were joined. Greek and Hebrew: none on this page. The page number is in a stylised old-style form; read as 263. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
